types.name: Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA)
types.purpose: Flying to or through Canada as a visitor, for visa-exempt nationalities.
types.who: Nationals of visa-exempt countries flying in
types.maxValidity: Up to 5 years (or until the passport expires)
types.note: Not a visa. The border officer decides how long you may stay, usually up to 6 months.

types.name: Visitor visa (temporary resident visa)
types.purpose: Tourism, visiting family or friends, for nationalities that need a visa.
types.who: Nationals of countries that need a visa
types.maxValidity: Up to 10 years or until the passport expires
types.note: The border officer decides how long you may stay, usually up to 6 months; the date may be stamped in your passport or on a visitor record.

types.name: Business visitor
types.purpose: Business meetings, conferences, trade shows and events, without entering the Canadian labour market.
types.maxValidity: Uses your eTA or visitor visa

types.name: Parent and grandparent super visa
types.purpose: Parents and grandparents visiting children or grandchildren who are Canadian citizens or permanent residents.
types.note: Up to 5 years at a time per entry.

types.name: Transit visa
types.purpose: Travelling through a Canadian airport to another country within 48 hours, for nationalities that need a visa.

types.name: Visitor record (extend your stay)
types.purpose: Staying longer in Canada as a visitor than the date you were given.

types.name: Study permit
types.purpose: Studying at a designated learning institution for longer than 6 months.
types.who: Students accepted by a designated school
types.maxValidity: Length of the program plus 90 days
types.note: Allows some work while you study, with conditions.

types.name: Post-graduation work permit
types.purpose: Working in Canada after graduating from an eligible Canadian program.
types.who: Graduates of an eligible Canadian program
types.maxValidity: Up to 3 years, depending on the program

types.name: Employer-specific work permit
types.purpose: Working for one employer under the conditions on your permit (often needs an LMIA).
types.who: Workers with a job offer (often an LMIA)
types.maxValidity: As on the permit (usually the length of the job offer)

types.name: Open work permit
types.purpose: Working for almost any employer — e.g. spouses of skilled workers or students, people waiting for permanent residence.
types.who: Spouses, graduates and other eligible groups

types.name: International Experience Canada (working holiday, young professionals, co-op)
types.purpose: Young people (usually 18–35) from partner countries travelling and working in Canada.
types.maxValidity: Usually 12 to 24 months, depending on your country

types.name: Work permit while waiting for permanent residence
types.purpose: Working while your permanent residence application is processed (bridging open work permit).

types.name: Open work permit for family of foreign workers
types.purpose: Spouses, common-law partners and dependent children of foreign workers in Canada.
types.who: Family of foreign workers in Canada

types.name: Express Entry (permanent residence)
types.purpose: Skilled workers: Federal Skilled Worker, Canadian Experience Class and Federal Skilled Trades.
types.who: Skilled workers who meet the points cut-off

types.name: Provincial Nominee Program
types.purpose: Permanent residence nominated by a province or territory for its labour needs.

types.name: Atlantic Immigration Program
types.purpose: Permanent residence with a job offer in New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, PEI or Newfoundland and Labrador.
types.who: Workers with a job offer in Atlantic Canada

types.name: Rural and Francophone Community Immigration Pilots
types.purpose: Permanent residence with a job in a participating rural or francophone community.
types.who: Workers with a job in a participating community

types.name: Quebec-selected skilled workers, investors and entrepreneurs
types.purpose: Permanent residence through selection by Quebec.

types.name: Caregivers (permanent residence)
types.purpose: Home child-care and home support workers.

types.name: Medical doctors (permanent residence)
types.purpose: Physicians with Canadian work experience.

types.name: Family sponsorship
types.purpose: Spouses, partners, dependent children, parents and grandparents sponsored by a Canadian citizen or permanent resident.
types.who: Family of Canadian citizens or residents

types.name: Start-up Visa / Self-employed persons
types.purpose: Entrepreneurs with an innovative business, or self-employed people in culture or athletics.
types.note: Both programs were paused when last checked.

types.name: Permanent resident card
types.purpose: Proof of permanent resident status for travelling back to Canada.
types.note: No day count, but you must live in Canada at least 730 days in every 5 years to keep the status.
